The season began on 24 January and ended on 6 December 2025.{{cite web|url=https://meridiano.net/futbol/futbol-venezolano/la-temporada-2025-de-la-liga-futve-ya-tiene-fecha-de-inicio-2024121916460|title=La temporada 2025 de la Liga FUTVE ya tiene fecha de inicio|trans-title=Liga FUTVE's 2025 season already has a start date|publisher=[[Diario Meridiano]]|language=es|date=19 December 2024|access-date=21 December 2024}} [[Universidad Central de Venezuela F.C.|Universidad Central]] were the champions, winning their fourth league title, second in the professional era and first since [[1957 Venezuelan Primera División season|1957]] after winning the Torneo Apertura and defeating [[Carabobo F.C.|Carabobo]] in the season's grand final.{{cite web|url=https://www.liderendeportes.com/noticias/futbol/futve/la-espera-termino-ucv-es-el-campeon-de-la-liga-futve-2025/|title=¡La espera terminó! UCV es el campeón de la Liga Futve 2025|trans-title=The wait is over! UCV are the 2025 Liga Futve champions|publisher=Líder en Deportes|language=es|date=6 December 2025|access-date=6 December 2025}} [[Deportivo Táchira F.C.|Deportivo Táchira]] were the defending champions, having won the title in the previous two seasons. ==Teams== Fourteen teams competed in the season, subject to the fulfillment of club licensing requirements: the top 13 teams of the 2024 season as well as the 2024 [[Venezuelan Segunda División|Segunda División]] champions [[Yaracuyanos F.C.|Yaracuyanos]], who defeated [[Anzoátegui F.C.|Anzoátegui]] in the Segunda División final on 30 November 2024.{{cite web|url=https://www.lavinotinto.com/yaracuyanos-fc-campeon-de-la-liga-futve-2-de-2024/|title=Yaracuyanos FC campeón de la Liga Futve 2 de 2024|trans-title=Yaracuyanos FC 2024 Liga Futve 2 champion|publisher=La Vinotinto|language=es|date=30 November 2024|access-date=21 December 2024}} Yaracuyanos replaced [[Inter de Barinas]], relegated at the end of the previous season after finishing last in the aggregate table. Following the end of the 2024 season, it was reported that [[Angostura F.C.|Angostura]] and the Segunda División runners-up Anzoátegui were negotiating a merger, with which Anzoátegui would take Angostura's place in Primera División.{{cite web|url=https://www.balonazos.com/adios-al-angostura-fc-y-bienvenido-el-anzoategui-fc-a-la-primera-division-de-la-liga-futve/|title=Adiós al Angostura FC y bienvenido el Anzoátegui FC a la primera división de la Liga FutVe|trans-title=Goodbye to Angostura FC and welcome Anzoátegui FC to the Liga FutVe's first division|publisher=Balonazos|language=es|date=20 December 2024|access-date=14 January 2025}} On 14 January 2025, the Liga FUTVE informed that Anzoátegui would replace Angostura in the tournament, but the latter club would take the former's spot in Segunda División.{{cite web|url=https://www.liderendeportes.com/noticias/destacado/todo-listo-para-el-inicio-de-la-liga-futve-2025/|title=Todo listo para el inicio de la Liga FUTVE 2025|trans-title=Everything set for the start of the 2025 Liga FUTVE|publisher=Líder en Deportes|language=es|date=14 January 2025|access-date=14 January 2025}} Four days later, the [[Venezuelan Football Federation]] confirmed that Angostura failed to comply with the financial requirements for a club license, whilst Anzoátegui had a higher sporting merit and had also fully met the licensing criteria.{{cite web|url=https://www.lavinotinto.com/angostura-fc-perdio-la-categoria-por-no-cumplir-con-la-licencia-de-clubes/|title=Angostura FC perdió la categoría por no cumplir con la Licencia de Clubes|trans-title=Angostura FC were relegated for not fulfilling the Clubs License|publisher=La Vinotinto|language=es|date=18 January 2025|access-date=10 July 2025}} {{Location map+ |Venezuela |float=right |width=450 |caption=Locations of the 2025 Primera División teams |places= {{Location map~ |Venezuela |lat=10.46840 |long=-68.0100 |label=
